skill_traces.query:
Tim: Hey John! It's been ages since we last talked. Guess what? Last week I went to a Harry Potter conference in the UK - it was incredible! There were so many people who shared the same love of HP as me, it was like a magical family. I felt so inspired and like I got a new lease of life. I love how my passion for fantasy stuff brings me closer to people from all over the world, it's pretty cool.
John: Hey Tim! Great to hear from you. It's awesome how our passions connect us with others, yeah? You sound like you fit right in and got a real buzz out of it. I feel the same way with my team.
Tim: Wow, you guys look great! How have games been going?
John: It was an intense season with both tough losses and great wins. Overall, I'd say we did pretty well.
Tim: Cool! Sounds like you guys had some tough games. How did you handle those?
John: Thanks! We faced tough opponents but that's what drives us to get better. We back each other up and won't quit.
Tim: Congrats! That's awesome. It must feel good, right?
John: Yeah, it feels great! All that hard work and effort was totally worth it. We even won a trophy!
Tim: Way to go! You must have been elated up there with that trophy. All the hard work paid off! Congrats - I'm so proud of you. Keep it up!
John: Thanks! I was definitely elated. Your support really means a lot to me. I'll keep working hard.
Tim: No problem! I'm here for you anytime. Keep believing in yourself!
John: Thanks! Appreciate your support. Always staying filled with self-belief.
Tim: You got this! Stay motivated and remember that anything is possible with hard work. Keep pushing for your goals!
John: Thanks! Your encouragement means a lot to me. I'm feeling motivated and ready to keep pushing for my goals! I'm going to need some new shoes after all these games though.
Tim: Glad my encouragement helped! These are amazing - like walking on clouds! Game changer!
John: They look comfortable. Where did you get them?
Tim: I got them online - they're super comfy! Definitely recommend!
John: Cheers! I'll definitely check them out. Thanks for the recommendation!
Tim: No worries. Let me know if there's anything else I can assist you with. Always here to help!
John: Thanks! Appreciate it. I'll reach out if I need anything.
Tim: Cool! Stay motivated and keep chasing those dreams! Chat soon!
John: Thanks! I'll definitely stay motivated and keep chasing those dreams. You too, keep up the passion. Talk soon!

selected.name: Extract Comfort and Joy Sources
selected.description: Use when a message states that something cheers the user up, brings joy, or provides comfort.
content: During extraction, if the user mentions a pet, hobby, person, item, or activity that provides cheer, comfort, or emotional support, create a separate durable memory (preference, relationship, or state) capturing that source, even when the message also contains stress or negative events.
Do not merge the supportive source only into a negative-event candidate; it should be its own candidate so it survives later SKIP/MERGE decisions.
Extract only sources explicitly stated as supportive; do not infer unmentioned ones.
selected.rerank_reason: The message contains explicit mentions of comfort and joy sources such as the Harry Potter conference, new shoes, and Tim's encouragement, which provide emotional support and cheer.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Inspiration and Plan Memories
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a user mentions what inspired or motivated their current or future project.
content: During extraction, treat statements like 'X sparked ideas for my [project]' as a plan/state memory candidate.
Do not skip a turn just because it contains no direct question; extract motivation and project details from casual narrative.
Resolve relative time from the message/session timestamp and include it in the memory.

nearby_not_selected.name: Capture Brief Project Mentions with Full Attributes
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a speaker mentions a project they completed, are working on, or plan to build, even briefly.
content: Create an event candidate for any explicit statement of a completed, ongoing, or planned project, even in small talk.
When several messages describe the same project, consolidate them into one candidate and include every explicit attribute stated.
Stop once the speaker has finished describing the project in that session.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Concrete Activity from Follow-Up Clarification
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a message describes an activity vaguely and the next message names the concrete result.
content: During extraction, treat any message reporting the speaker performing an activity as a candidate source, even when the object is only a photo or pronoun.
If the following message from another participant identifies the concrete object or result, extract an event memory capturing who did what, using both messages as evidence.
Do not skip follow-up messages that clarify or name an earlier activity.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Start of Specific Creative Work
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a user confirms starting or recently beginning a specific creative work.
content: When a message confirms a user is working on a specific creative work with an ordinal or title and a beginning phrase, add an event memory with subject=user and world_start set to the message date.
Treat recent-start statements as start events; do not mark completion unless explicitly stated.
Prefer this specific event memory over a generic profile enrichment.

nearby_not_selected.name: Capture likely deceased from euphemistic absence language
nearby_not_selected.description: During extraction, when a speaker describes someone with euphemistic absence language (e.g., 'will never be able to...', 'I miss him/her here') that strongly implies death, use this guidance.
content: When a statement euphemistically implies a person has died without explicitly saying so, also extract the implied state that the person is likely deceased, in addition to the literal statement.
Record the inference with an appropriate hedge (e.g., 'likely deceased') because the speaker did not state it directly; do not assert cause, date, or circumstances of death.
Stop after capturing the likely-deceased state and the literal content; do not extrapolate further details about the person or the relationship.
